original_value: Stragglers are exceptionally slow tasks within a job that delay its completion. Stragglers, which are uncommon within a single job, are pervasive in datacenters with many jobs. A large body of research has focused on mitigating datacenter stragglers, but relatively little research has focused on systematically and rigorously identifying their root causes. We present Hound, a statistical machine learning framework that infers the causes of stragglers from traces of datacenter-scale jobs. Hound is designed to achieve several objectives: datacenter-scale diagnosis, interpretable models, unbiased inference, and computational efficiency. We demonstrate Hound's capabilities for a production trace from Google's warehouse-scale datacenters and two Spark traces from Amazon EC2 clusters.

result.paraphrase: Stragglers are unusually slow tasks in a job that hold up its completion. Although they are rare in a single job, they are widespread across datacenters running many jobs. Much research has aimed to reduce datacenter stragglers, but comparatively little has systematically and rigorously identified their root causes. We introduce Hound, a statistical machine learning framework that infers the causes of stragglers from traces of datacenter-scale jobs. Hound is built to provide datacenter-scale diagnosis, interpretable models, unbiased inference, and computational efficiency. We show Hound’s capabilities on a production trace from Google’s warehouse-scale datacenters and two Spark traces from Amazon EC2 clusters.
